rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayb names what is wholly absent from sense and reason; one class has no evidence and is known only to God, while another is inferable and is intended here.
rows.anchor: والغيب مصدر سمي به الغائب توسعا كقولهم للزائر : زور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inferable unseen includes the Creator and His attributes, prophethood and its laws, and the resurrection, accounting, and recompense.
rows.anchor: قسم نصب عليه دليل كالصانع وصفاته والنبوات وما يتعلق بها من الأحكام والشرائع واليوم الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed bāʾ may mark belief by construing īmān as acknowledgment or as trust, with the unseen as its object; alternatively it may introduce a circumstantial phrase describing believers.
rows.anchor: فالباء صلة الإيمان إما بتضمينه معنى الاعتراف أو بجعله مجازا عن الوثوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the circumstantial reading, believers are absent from the Prophet and his signs, or absent from other people, unlike hypocrites who privately claim loyalty to their own group.
rows.anchor: غائبين عن المؤمنين لا كالمنافقين الذين

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd answers Ḥārith b. Nughayr that believers can count the Companions’ vision and companionship as their distinction, while the Companions count unseen faith as theirs; he calls it the best faith.
rows.anchor: فقال عبد الله : ونحن نحتسب لكم إيمانكم به ولم تروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading takes the unseen to mean the hidden heart: faith is held inwardly, unlike hypocrites’ words that contradict their hearts.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالغيب القلب لأنه مستور

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿUmar reports the famous questioning of the Prophet by a stranger about Islam, faith, excellence, the Hour, and its signs; the excerpt breaks off as the first sign is introduced.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : بينا نحن عند رسول الله

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The Mathnawī couplets commend love and companionship with people of heart, whose hidden worth is known to God.
rows.anchor: قال في "المثنوي" : مهر ا كان درميان جان نشان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The encounter verse explains how hypocrites treated believers and unbelievers and prepares the account of their hypocrisy; it is not a repetition.
rows.anchor: بيان لمعاملتهم مع المؤمنين والكفار وما صدرت به القصة فمساقه لبيان مذهبهم وتمهيد نفاقهم فليس بتكرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers they meet are the Muhājirūn and Anṣār, whom the hypocrites falsely greet as though sharing their faith.
rows.anchor: واستقبلوا الذين آمنوا بالحق وهم المهاجرون والأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An account depicts Ibn Ubayy greeting Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿAlī with lavish praise, then assuring ʿAlī that his faith matches theirs while feigning Muslim loyalty.
rows.anchor: روي أن عبد الله بن أبي المنافق وأصحابه خرجوا ذات يوم فاستقبلهم نفر من الصحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlī warns Ibn Ubayy against hypocrisy; after the groups part, Ibn Ubayy asks his companions how he handled the encounter and tells them to imitate him.
rows.anchor: يا عبد الله اتق الله ولا تنافق فإن المنافقين شر خلق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about withdrawing to them can mean departing, privately meeting, or being alone; ilā may function like maʿa or bāʾ, as in the idiom for being alone with someone.
rows.anchor: مضوا أو اجتمعوا على الخلوة وإلى بمعنى مع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their satans are associates who resemble Satan in rebellion and publicly reveal disbelief; the term can also distinguish senior hypocrites from the junior ones who speak.
rows.anchor: أصحابهم المماثلين للشيطان في التمرد والعناد المظهرين لكفرهم وإضافتهم إليه للمشاركة في الكفر

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies their satans as soothsayers: Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf among Qurayẓa, Abū Burda among Aslam, ʿAbd al-Dār among Juhayna, ʿAwf b. ʿĀmir among Asad, and ʿAbd Allāh b. Sawdāʾ in Syria.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك المراد بشياطينهم كهنتهم وهم في بني قريظة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Arabs believed soothsayers knew the unseen and secrets and treated the ill; each soothsayer had a satan who supplied divinations, and they were called satans for being far from truth.
rows.anchor: وكانت العرب تعتقد فيهم أنهم مطلعون على الغيب ويعرفون الأسرار ويداوون المرضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites’ private claim means they remain companions and agree in religion and belief, never leaving their faction.
rows.anchor: إنا مصاحبوكم وموافقوكم على دينكم واعتقادكم لا نفارقكم في حال من الأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their profession of Islam before believers is only a show: it secures spoils, marriages, intelligence, and protection for their families and property, while they ridicule the believers.
rows.anchor: وإنما نكون معهم ظاهرا لنشاركهم في غنائمهم وننكح بناتهم ونطلع على أسرارهم ونحفظ أموالنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istehzāʾ means treating someone as ignorant, mocking, or belittling him; the hypocrites say they display Islam only to deride Muḥammad and his Companions.
rows.anchor: والاستهزاء التجهيل والسخرية والاستخفاف والمعنى أنا نجهل محمدا وأصحابه ونسخر بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should not be dazzled by long life or abundant wealth and children: God may extend these to enemies as a form of abandonment and deprivation.
rows.anchor: أن العبد ينبغي له أن لا يغتر بطول العمر وامتداده ولا بكثرة أمواله وأولاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extension given to enemies is answered by extended punishment, while God gives His friend extended shade in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقد جعل الله لعدوه في الدنيا مالا ممدودا ولوليه في الآخرة ظلا ممدودا

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: A saying attributed to God at the Ascension explains that the community’s shorter lives, smaller fortunes, and later era reduce sins, accounting, and confinement in graves.
rows.anchor: وقال الله جل جلاله لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة المعراج

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: Another Ascension saying warns Aḥmad against luxury because the ego is a source of evil: it resists obedience, obeys sin, grows tyrannical when full, and forgets when reminded.
rows.anchor: وروي أن الله تعالى قال لحبيبه ليلة المعراج :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative points emphatically to the hypocrites and signals their remote, exceptionally evil condition; it is the subject whose predicate is that they exchanged misguidance for guidance.
rows.anchor: المنافقون المتصفون بما ذكر من الصفات الشنيعة المميزة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buying first means paying a price, then metaphorically giving up what one holds to obtain something else; here they chose unbelief and deviation instead of faith and the straight path.
rows.anchor: أصل الاشتراء بذل الثمن لتحصيل ما يطلب من الأشياء ثم استعير للإعراض عما في يده محصلا به غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an exchange, bāʾ accompanies what is relinquished; this supports establishing a legal ruling through conduct without spoken offer and acceptance.
rows.anchor: والباء تصحب المتروك في باب المعارضة وهذا دليل على أن الحكم يثبت بالتعاطي من غير تكلم بالإيجاب والقبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the trade unprofitable extends the metaphor: profit belongs literally to traders, but is attributed to their trade as its agent or cause; the fa implies that their purchase yielded no gain.
rows.anchor: فإن الربح مسند إلى أرباب التجارة في الحقيقة فإسناده إلى التجارة نفسها على الاتساع لتلبسها بالفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trade seeks a surplus over its capital; even a lost deal can be recovered while capital remains, but the hypocrites destroyed both their sound nature and clear reason, leaving no means to reach truth or perfection.
rows.anchor: فإن المقصد منها سلامة رأس المال مع حصول الربح ولئن فات الربح في صفقة فربما يتدارك في صفقة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True guidance requires leaving worldly habits for obedience and worship, rather than following every desire and mixing whim with guidance.
rows.anchor: هو الذي ترك الدنيا والعادة ثم اشتغل بوظائف الطاعة والعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Daqqāq tells a wealthy disciple that voluntary night prayer will not cure him while love of worldly life remains; he must first remove that love, then take up extra worship.
rows.anchor: حكي أنه كان للشيخ الأستاذ أبي علي الدقاق رضي الله عنه مريد تاجر متمول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shaykh compares misdirected spiritual treatment to applying ointment to a foot for a headache or washing a garment’s hem to cleanse a dirty hand.
rows.anchor: فمن كان به أذى من رأسه من صداع لا يسكن ألمه بالطلاء على الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Squandering the two gains leaves a complete veil from God, rusting over the heart, as the Qurʾān says.
rows.anchor: وخسرانهم بإضاعة الأمرين هو الحجاب الكلي عن الحق بالرين

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Their tyranny and confusion make them content with worldly life and saturate their hearts with misguidance; the resulting state comes from their own transaction.
rows.anchor: التأويلات النجمية" الإشارة في الآية أن من نتيجة طغيانهم

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: They gave up their capacity to receive guidance, so they cannot regain it; preferring the world to the afterlife is a loss, but preferring both to God is worse, leaving them captive to desire and cut off from the Beloved.
rows.anchor: لأنهم أخرجوا استعداد قبول الهداية عن قدرتهم وتصرفهم فلا يملكون الرجوع إليه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: They are not guided because they invalidated their good innate readiness to accept guidance.
rows.anchor: لإبطالهم حسن استعداد قبول الهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Breaking God’s covenant means opposing and abandoning His command; naqḍ literally means undoing or unfastening a joined structure.
rows.anchor: يخالفون ويتركون أمر الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling covenant-breaking ‘undoing’ is apt because covenant is metaphorically a rope that secures a bond between the parties.
rows.anchor: من حيث تسميتهم العهد بالحبل على سبيل الاستعارة لما فيه من ثبات الوصلة بين المتعاهدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account counts three covenants: Adam’s descendants acknowledge God’s lordship, prophets establish religion without division, and scholars disclose rather than conceal truth.
rows.anchor: قيل : عهد الله ثلاثة : الأول ما أخذه على ذرية آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘after its covenant’ may refer to the covenant itself, or to God who confirmed it by sending scriptures and messengers; mīthāq can mean the act of confirmation.
rows.anchor: فالضمير للعهد أو بعد توثيق الله ذلك بإنزال الكتب وإرسال الرسل فالضمير إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mālik b. Dīnār recounts a cousin who repeatedly vowed to leave an oppressive sultan’s service when ill, broke each vow after recovery, and died after a final divine rebuke called him a liar.
rows.anchor: يحكى عن مالك بن دينار رحمه الله أنه كان له ابن عم عامل سلطان في زمانهم وكان ظالما جائرا

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The Mathnawī says breaking covenants and vows ultimately brings a curse.
rows.anchor: قال في "المثنوي" : نقض ميثاق وشكست توبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, ‘to be joined’ is an appositive to the relative object; its scope includes every rupture God disapproves: kinship, solidarity among believers, affirming prophets and scriptures together, congregational duties, and abandoning good or doing evil.
rows.anchor: محل أن يوصل النصب على أنه بدل من ضمير الموصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such ruptures sever the intended bond between God and servant, which is the purpose underlying every joining and separation.
rows.anchor: فإنه يقطع ما بين الله تعالى وبين العبد من الوصلة التي هي المقصودة بالذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report warns that people who display knowledge but neglect it, love with their tongues but hate in their hearts, and sever kinship incur God’s curse and loss of hearing and sight.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "إذا أظهر الناس العلم وضيعوا العمل به

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises divine shade to a widow who raises her young orphans rather than remarrying, a wealthy person who feeds orphans and the poor, and one who maintains kinship; the last receives expanded provision and lifespan.
rows.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم "ثلاثة في ظل عرش الله يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Corruption in the land consists of blocking faith, mocking truth, and cutting the ties that sustain worldly order and flourishing.
rows.anchor: بالمنع عن الإيمان والاستهزاء بالحق وقطع الوصل التي عليها يدور فلك نظام العالم وصلاحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The losers trade fidelity for breach, connection for severance, rectitude for corruption, and reward for punishment.
rows.anchor: لأنهم استبدلوا النقض بالوفاء والقطع بالوصل والفساد بالصلاح وعقابها بثوابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said that every person has a home, family, and servants in Paradise; the obedient reaches them, while the disobedient loses them to a believer and is cheated of his share.
rows.anchor: قيل : ليس من مؤمن ولا كافر إلا وله منزل وأهل

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: People of faith see realities and meanings through parables, whereas deniers’ rejection darkens their sight, so they cannot see truth clothed in Arabic imagery and ask what God intends.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {إن الله لا يستحى أن يضرب مثلا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says creation began in darkness and God sprinkled it with light; those touched by the light were guided, while those it missed went astray.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "إن الله خلق الخلق في ظلمة ثم رش عليهم من نوره

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Those who missed the primordial light also miss faith and Qurʾānic light; those who received it receive both, since the Qurʾān brings healing and mercy to some and misery and punishment to others.
rows.anchor: فمن أخطأه ذلك النور في عالم الأرواح فقد أخطأه نور الإيمان ههنا ومن أخطأه نور الإيمان

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: As God’s speech and attribute, the Qurʾān combines gentleness and severity: through gentleness it guides the sincere and through severity misguides transgressors.
rows.anchor: وكان القرآن لقوم شفاء ورحمة ولقوم شقاء ونقمة لأنه كلامه ، وصفته

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The primordial covenant bound people to monotheism and sincere servitude; severing means cutting the paths of spiritual wayfaring to God and retreat from creation.
rows.anchor: يوم الميثاق على التوحيد والعبودية بالإخلاص من بعد ميثاقه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The paths to be joined are means of spiritual wayfaring and withdrawal from creation toward God.
rows.anchor: من أسباب السلوك الموصل إلى الحق وأسباب التبتل والانقطاع عن الخلق

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: They corrupt the innate seed of monotheism by associating partners and rejecting the prophets, failing to water it with faith and righteous deeds; thus they lose human perfection as a seed loses its potential without water.
rows.anchor: يفسدون بذر التوحيد الفطري في أرض طينتهم بالشرك والإعراض عن قبول دعوة الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Abraham perfected himself, he perfected others through a gracious recommendation of what benefits them, whether religious or worldly.
rows.anchor: لما كمل إبراهيم عليه السلام في نفسه كمل غيره بالتوصية وهو تقديم ما فيه خير وصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘It’ refers to the religion in the preceding mention of Abraham’s way.
rows.anchor: بالملة المذكورة في قوله تعالى : {ومن يرغب عن ملة إبراهام}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some count Abraham’s eight sons as Ishmael by Hājar, Isaac by Sarah, and six sons by Keturah: Midian, Midain, Zimran, Yaqshan, Yashbaq, and Nuh.
rows.anchor: أولاده الذكور الثمانية عند البعض إسماعيل وأمه هاجر القبطية وإسحاق وأمه سارة وستة أمهم قنطورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob also advised his twelve sons; the commentary names them and explains his name by saying he followed his twin Esau out of the womb holding his heel.
rows.anchor: أيضا وهو ابن إسحاق بن إبراهيم بنيه الاثني عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A birth story has the twins speak in the womb: Esau demands to emerge first, Jacob yields to avoid harming their mother, and Jacob comes out holding Esau’s heel; Esau grows harsh and hunts, Jacob gentle and pastoral.
rows.anchor: تكلما في بطنها وهي تسمع فقال أحدهما للآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob and Esau reportedly died on the same day and were buried together; Jacob lived 147 years, died in Egypt, and asked Joseph to bury him in the Holy Land by Isaac.
rows.anchor: وروي أنهما ماتا في يوم واحد ودفنا في قبر واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative ‘my sons’ is governed by an understood verb of saying, since Basran grammarians do not allow a full sentence to be the object except with verbs of thought or speech.
rows.anchor: على إضمار القول عند البصريين تقديره وصى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chose Islam as the purest religion; the prohibition against dying except as Muslims really commands steadfastness in Islam, sincere monotheism, and good expectation of God, since people cannot control death.
rows.anchor: دين الإسلام الذي هو صفوة الأديان ولا دين عنده غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob stressed this to his sons after seeing Egyptian idol worship; he singled out his beloved family to show Islam’s priority and because a sound leader’s family helps make the community sound.
rows.anchor: وذلك حين دخل يعقوب مصر فرأى أهلها يعبدون الأصنام فأوصى بنيه بأن يثبتوا على الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening am is disconnected, equivalent to bal plus a hamza; al-Taysīr says that without a preceding interrogative alif it is a direct denial, asking whether they were witnesses and answering that they were not present.
rows.anchor: وأم منقطعة مقدرة ببل والهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s ‘coming of death’ means its signs, causes, and nearness, not the instant of death itself.
rows.anchor: إماراته وأسبابه وقرب خروجه من الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers Jews who claimed Jacob instructed his sons to follow Judaism at death: they were absent, and Jacob in fact urged Islam.
rows.anchor: نزلت حين قالت اليهود للنبي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob asked what his sons would worship after him to reaffirm their monotheism and Islam and secure their pledge to remain steadfast.
rows.anchor: أي شيء تعبدونه بعد موتي أراد به تقريرهم على التوحيد

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says the question covers more than formal worship: every act should seek God’s face and pleasure, avoiding whatever does not lead to Him; Jacob feared worldly distraction more than idols.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب لم يعن بقوله : ما تعبدون من بعدي العبادة المشروعة فقط

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The Mathnawī teaches that worldly possessions distract from God; the problem is heedlessness, not fabric, silver, or the number and weight of children themselves.
rows.anchor: قال في "المثنوي" : يست دنيا از خدا غافل شدن

rows.speaker: التفتازاني
rows.claim: Al-Taftāzānī says mā can refer to rational or nonrational things while they are unspecified; once rationality is known, man is used for the rational and mā for other things.
rows.anchor: قال النحرير التفتازاني : وما عام أي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sons say they will worship the one God worshipped by their forefathers, acknowledged in existence, divinity, and entitlement to worship; Ishmael, though Jacob’s uncle, is included as a father because an uncle is like a father.
rows.anchor: نعبد الإله المتفق على وجوده وإلهيته ووجوب عبادته

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet compares a man’s paternal uncle to his father’s twin, just as two palm shoots are paired.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : "عم الرجل صنو أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘One God’ is either an appositive to the God of the forefathers or an expression of specification; it states monotheism and removes ambiguity from repeating the possessive.
rows.anchor: بدل من إله آبائك وفائدته التصريح بالتوحيد ودفع التوهم الناشىء من تكرار المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘We submit to Him’ is a circumstantial clause describing the subject of ‘we worship.’
rows.anchor: مسلمون} حال من فاعل نعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That community’ points to Abraham, Jacob, and their monotheistic descendants; umma first means an intended goal and then a group people aim at and follow.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى الأمة المذكورة التي هي إبراهيم ويعقوب وبنوهما الموحدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community ‘passed away’ by dying and became separate from others; the expression derives from becoming empty or uninhabited.
rows.anchor: مضت بالموت وانفردت عمن عداها وأصله صارت إلى الخلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each community receives only its own deeds, not another’s; the fronted phrase marks exclusivity and denies both inheriting past people’s reward and bearing their sins.
rows.anchor: لها كسبها لا كسب غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews argued that descent from Jacob should benefit them despite his religion; the response is that lineage cannot replace following his deeds.
rows.anchor: وذلك لما ادعى اليهود أن يعقوب عليه السلام مات على اليهودية وأنه عليه السلام وصى بها بنيه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet tells Banū Hāshim not to rely on lineage while others bring their deeds, and says that a person held back by his deeds will not be advanced by his ancestry.
rows.anchor: يا بني هاشم لا يأتيني الناس بأعمالهم وتأتوني بأنسابكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem likewise says that a noble lineage does not benefit its possessor.
rows.anchor: أتفخر باتصالك من علي وأصل البؤسة الماء القراح وليس بنافع نسب زكي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet remarked on a woman’s beautiful white teeth to teach that one should mention the best quality of anything.
rows.anchor: فقال عليه السلام : ما أحسن بياض أسنانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage concerns Jewish scholars who expected the prophet described in the Torah to come from their own people; when Muḥammad came from elsewhere, they altered and concealed the description to preserve their authority.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أحبار اليهود فإنهم كانوا يرجون أن يكون النبي المنعوت في التوراة منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘What God sent down from the Book’ is a circumstantial phrase for the omitted object; the Book is the Torah containing the Prophet’s description.
rows.anchor: أنزل الله حال كونه من الكتاب وهو التوراة المشتمل على نعت محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The small price is what they take from their followers as food in exchange for concealing revelation.
rows.anchor: المآكل التي يصيبونها من سفلتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their food is literally fire in the afterlife; in this life it is called fire as the cause leading to punishment, and ‘in their bellies’ implies that they fill them completely.
rows.anchor: أما في الآخرة فظاهر لأنهم لا يأكلون يوم القيامة إلا عين النار عقوبة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s refusal to speak to them means no merciful speech, not absolute silence, which would conflict with the statement that all will be questioned.
rows.anchor: فليس المراد به نفي الكلام حقيقة لئلا يتعارض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He will neither praise them nor cleanse their sins as He cleanses believers; their punishment is painful and lasting.
rows.anchor: لا يثني عليهم ولا يطهرهم من دنس الذنوب يوم يطهر المؤمنين من ذنوبهم بالمغفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not literally buy a price: with respect to this life they gave up guidance for misguidance, and with respect to the next they exchanged forgiveness for punishment.
rows.anchor: بالنسبة إلى الدنيا {الضلالة} التي ليست مما يمكن أن يشتري قطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘How patient they are over the Fire’ marvels at their persistence in deeds that lead to it; Fire names its cause, and the astonishment belongs to human hearers, since divine astonishment would imply ignorance.
rows.anchor: ما أصبرهم على أعمال أهل النار حين تركوا الهدى وسلكوا مسالك الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment follows because God sent scripture with truth, so rejecting or concealing it and embracing ignorance warrants forms of torment.
rows.anchor: بسبب أنه {نزل الكتاب} أي : جنس الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disagreement about scripture means accepting some divine books and rejecting others, accepting some Torah verses but rejecting the altered prophecies of Muḥammad, or calling the Qurʾān poetry, sorcery, or soothsaying.
rows.anchor: بأن آمنوا ببعض كتب الله وكفروا ببعضها أو في التوراة بأن آمنوا ببعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses severely warn scholars not to hide truth for worldly advantage, fear of losing status, desire for favors or office, or shared attachment to luxury and leadership; such people consume the fire of greed, envy, and desire, which devours good deeds.
rows.anchor: لكل من يكتم الحق لغرض فاسد دنيوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators agree that those who disobeyed returned home; the preferred view is that they turned back before crossing the river, since only Saul and the obedient believers crossed it.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه لا خلاف بين المفسرين في أن الذين عصوا رجعوا إلى بلدهم والصحيح أنهم لم يجاوزوا النهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among those who crossed, one group loved life and feared death, declaring they could not face Goliath’s army, said to number one hundred thousand armed soldiers.
rows.anchor: والقسم الأول هم الذين قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second, brave group answers that many small companies have defeated larger ones by God’s permission; divine support, not numbers, determines victory, and God supports the patient.
rows.anchor: والقسم الثاني : هم الذين أجابوهم بقولهم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib reads the story as an example of worldly life: taking enough for need brings safety, while taking more increases thirst; a person’s greed ends only in the grave unless he repents.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : في القصة إيماء ومثال للدنيا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says that even two valleys of gold would make Adam’s child seek a third; only earth fills him, and God accepts the repentance of one who turns back.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "لو أن لابن آدم واديين من ذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning Adam’s child hints at his earthly origin and grasping nature; divine enabling can soften it, so the sensible person need not exhaust himself collecting a provision that is already apportioned.
rows.anchor: وههنا نكتة وهي أن في ذكر ابن آدم دون الأنسال تلويحا إلى أنه مخلوق من تراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding Persian verses portray the spiritually realized as hidden and nameless, united in both outward religious law and inward truth.
rows.anchor: تنشان بشريعت هم دلشان بحقيقت هم هم دل شده وهم جان نه اين ونه آن مانده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentator prays for God’s peace and mercy and asks to be counted among those spiritually realized.
rows.anchor: عليهم سلام الله ورحمته وبركاته اللهم اجعلنا من اللاحقين بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saul and his believers emerge into the open battlefield, see the enemy’s forces and equipment, and collectively pray after the fearful group’s hearts have been strengthened by the brave.
rows.anchor: ظهر طالوت ومن معه من المؤمنين وصاروا إلى براز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God ‘our Lord’ acknowledges servitude and seeks their reform, since the word Lord conveys that relation.
rows.anchor: في ندائهم بقولهم {ربنا} اعتراف منهم بالعبودية وطلب لإصلاحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Pour upon us’ pictures abundance and completion of patience covering them like a vessel; they ask endurance for battle’s hardships.
rows.anchor: إفراغ الإناء إخلاؤه مما فيه أي : صب علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firm feet signify inner strength, resolve, and steadiness when confronting the enemy, not merely remaining in one physical place.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بثبات القدم كمال القوة والرسوخ عند المقارنة وعدم التزلزل وقت المقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prayer follows a deliberate order: abundant patience first, firmness arising from it second, and victory over the enemy as the ultimate aim.
rows.anchor: حيث قدموا سؤال إفراغ الصبر على قلوبهم الذي هو ملاك الأمر ثم سؤال تثبيت القدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stated due date should use days, months, years, or another precise measure; harvest, threshing, or a pilgrim’s arrival are too uncertain.
rows.anchor: بالأيام أو الأشهر أو السنة وغيرها مما يفيد العلم ويرفع الجهالة لا بالحصاد والدياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing the debt and its due date is safer and prevents disputes; the majority consider the command a recommendation.
rows.anchor: الدين بأجله لأنه أوثق وأدفع للنزاع والجمهور على استحبابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scribe should mediate between both parties and record what each says, in equal terms without favor, addition, or omission; they should choose a learned, religious jurist whose document is legally reliable.
rows.anchor: وقوله بينكم للإيذان بأن الكاتب ينبغي أن يتوسط بين المتداينين ويكتب كلامهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A scribe should not refuse to write the debt in the manner God taught for documenting agreements; the command reinforces the preceding prohibition.
rows.anchor: لا يمتنع أحد من الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor should dictate because he is the party answerable and must acknowledge the obligation.
rows.anchor: الإملال هو الإملاء وهو إلقاء المعنى على الكاتب للكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor is especially warned to fear God and not reduce the dictated amount, since self-protection gives him an incentive to understate what he owes.
rows.anchor: لما فيه من الدواعي إلى المنهى عنه فإن الإنسان مجبول على دفع الضرر عن نفسه وتخفيف ما في ذمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person unable to dictate may also be hindered by ignorance or another impediment; a guardian then takes over.
rows.anchor: أو جهل أو غير ذلك من العوارض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person’s guardian, administrator, proxy, or translator dictates fairly, without increasing or reducing the amount.
rows.anchor: أي : الذي يلي أمره ويقوم مقامه من قيم أو وكيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two male witnesses are sought to carry testimony about the transaction; they are called witnesses in anticipation of giving testimony later.
rows.anchor: أي : اطلبوهما ليتحملا الشهادة على ما جرى بينكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘From your men’ means free adult Muslims of your community; in transactions between unbelievers or where the debtor is an unbeliever, unbelievers may be witnesses according to the author’s school.
rows.anchor: من أهل دينكم يعني من الأحرار البالغين المسلمين إذ الكلام في معاملاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If two men are unavailable, one man and two women may witness financial matters by consensus; women do not testify in fixed punishments or retaliation, where men are required.
rows.anchor: وشهادة النساء مع الرجال في الأموال جائزة بالإجماع دون الحدود والقصاص فلا بد فيهما من الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requirement that witnesses be approved applies to both the man and the women; women are included by grammatical predominance, and the phrase points to trust and known integrity.
rows.anchor: كائنون مرضيين عندكم وتخصيصهم بالوصف المذكور مع تحقق اعتباره في كل شهيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One woman may forget and the other remind her; reminder is the real purpose, while possible error is named as its cause, as in preparing a weapon to repel a possible enemy.
rows.anchor: وهذا تعليل لاعتبار العدد في النساء والعلة في الحقيقة هي التذكير ولكن الضلال لما كان سببا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnesses should not refuse when summoned to give or bear testimony.
rows.anchor: ثم حث الشهداء على إقامة الشهادة بقوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not tire of documenting a debt, large or small, whether summarized or detailed, through its agreed due date.
rows.anchor: لا تملوا من كثرة مدايناتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Documenting it to the due date is fairest before God, strengthens testimony, and best prevents doubt about the debt, amount, term, or witnesses.
rows.anchor: أي : أعدل {عند الله} أي : في حكمه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Immediate exchange with both parties present may be left unwritten because hand-to-hand trade is less prone to dispute and forgetting.
rows.anchor: لكن وقت كون تداينكم أو تجارتكم تجارة حاضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witness sales either in this particular transaction or generally as a precaution; the majority take the verse’s commands as recommendations.
rows.anchor: أي : هذا التبايع أو مطلقا لأنه أحوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If active, the prohibition bars a scribe from refusing or altering the document and a witness from withholding testimony; if passive, it bars others from harming them while occupied or withholding their fee.
rows.anchor: كاتب} عن الكتابة المقصودة {ولا شهيد} أي : ولا يمتنع الشاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Violating the ban on harm is disobedience; believers should fear God in all His commands and prohibitions, and He teaches rulings that serve their interests and knows their conduct.
rows.anchor: في مخالفة أوامره ونواهيه التي من جملتها نهيه عن المضارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s detailed protection of people’s rights shows that safeguarding property is necessary; those who pursue truth are saved, while others stray.
rows.anchor: يعلم بذلك أن مراعاة حقوق الخلق واجبة والاحتياط على الأموال التي بها أمور الدين والدنيا لازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God teaches transaction rules out of mercy to prevent injustice, quarrels, resentment, and worldly distress; this shows that religious obligations also bring purification and blessing.
rows.anchor: والله تعالى من كمال رحمته على عباده علمهم كيفية معاملاتهم فيما بينهم لئلا يجري من بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first of three lessons concerns God’s relation to servants: His care in worldly dealings prevents loss and dispute and indicates that religious duties likewise express mercy and bring His blessings.
rows.anchor: فيشير بهذه المعاني إلى ثلاثة أحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second lesson concerns servants’ relation to God: carefulness over fleeting worldly transactions should teach even greater care over enduring afterlife matters, for every atom of good and evil is rewarded or punished.
rows.anchor: وثانيها حال العباد مع الله ليعلموا برعاية هذه الدقائق للأمور الدنيوية الفانية أن للأمور الأخروية الباقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s covenant with believers is a purchase of their lives and property for Paradise, witnessed by the angels; the written contract records a jewel from Paradise deposited as the Black Stone.
rows.anchor: فإن الله تعالى اشترى من المؤمنين أنفسهم وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة وعلى هذا عاهدهم وأشهد الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third lesson concerns people’s dealings with one another: imitate God’s gentleness, keep His limits in agreement and disagreement, love, accompany, guide, and advise one another for His sake.
rows.anchor: حال العباد فيما بينهم فليعتبر كل واحد منهم من ملاطفات الحق معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In all three conditions, remain mindful of God, who teaches through explicit statements and indications.
rows.anchor: كما قال : {واتقوا اللها ويعلمكم الله}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows hidden thoughts and secrets and rewards people according to the sincerity and purity of their intentions; blessed is the person who purifies his character and seeks the unseen.
rows.anchor: يعلم مضمون ضمائركم ومكنون سرائركم فيجازيكم على حسن معاملتكم بقدر خلوصكم وصفاء نياتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian poem compares the unseen to a decorated palace and desire to a cloud of dust: abandoning desire removes the screen and enables sight of the desired reality.
rows.anchor: حقائق سراييست آراسته هوا وهوس كرد برخاسته نه بيني كه جايى كه برخاست كرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being on a journey means traveling toward and turning to one’s destination; lacking a scribe includes lack of writing skill or writing materials, and the verse does not mention witnesses because their availability follows the same rationale.
rows.anchor: مسافرين أي : متوجهين إليه ومقبلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pledge is collateral that must be delivered to the lender; an undelivered pledge does not compel the pledgor to hand it over. Travel is mentioned because writing and witnesses are often unavailable, not because pledges are restricted to travel.
rows.anchor: جمع رهن أي : فالتوثق رهن

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet pawned his armor to a Jew in Medina for twenty measures of barley for his family.
rows.anchor: وقد رهن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم درعه في المدينة من يهودي بعشرين صاعا من شعير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the lender trusts the debtor and waives collateral, the debtor must repay the entrusted debt without delay; the debt is called a trust because it rests on his liability.
rows.anchor: وهو المديون والائتمان الوثوق بأمانة الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnesses must not conceal testimony when summoned; anyone concealing it commits a sin of the heart.
rows.anchor: أيها الشهود إذا دعيتم إلى الحاكم لأدائها على وجهها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sin is assigned to the heart because concealment begins by inwardly suppressing testimony; attributing an act to its working organ makes the charge more emphatic.
rows.anchor: كتمان الشهادة هو أن يضمرها ولا يتكلم بها فلما كان الإثم مقترفا بالقلب أسند إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart is the root and noblest seat of the self: its soundness or corruption governs the whole body, so the sin is not merely of the tongue, which only expresses it.
rows.anchor: ولأن القلب هو رأس الأعراض والمضغة التي إن صلحت صلح الجسد كله وإن فسدت فسد الجسد كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heart-actions are roots from which bodily deeds branch; faith and unbelief are the roots of good and evil, so concealment of testimony is a grave heart-sin.
rows.anchor: ولأن أفعال القلوب أعظم من أفعال سائر الجوارح وهي لها كالأصول التي تتشعب منها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās counts associating partners with God, false testimony, and concealing testimony among the greatest grave sins.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أكبر الكبائر الإشراك بالله لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows deeds and will repay good with good and evil with evil; false testimony and concealed testimony lead to Hell and reveal corruption of the heart, aided by common motives such as enmity.
rows.anchor: فيجازيكم به إن خيرا فخير وإن شرا فشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religious people are either stationary, confined to outward form with no access to inner meaning, or traveling from bodily form toward spiritual meaning; the stationary resemble a chick trapped in its shell and have scribes recording outward deeds.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن أهل الدين طائفتان الواقفون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A traveler moves from outward form and bodily confinement into inward meaning and the spacious realm of spirits; travelers are either walkers or flyers.
rows.anchor: والسائر من لم يقم ولم ينزل في منزل فهو مسافر من عالم الصورة إلى عالم المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The walker follows the path of the religious law and reason; the flyer moves on the wings of love and aspiration toward ultimate reality, while remaining tethered to the law.
rows.anchor: فالسيار من يسير بقدم الشرع والعقل على جادة الطريقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, the traveling walker is freed from bodily confinement, senses, and scribal surveillance; some mystics say the left recorder wrote nothing for twenty years, or that the right recorder asked to record heart-deeds and was told the obligations sufficed.
rows.anchor: إلى السيار الذي تخلص من سجن الجسد وقيد الحواس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pledge is the walker’s heart, kept for God alone and held between the fingers of the All-Merciful.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى اليسار الذي له قلب فيرهنه عند الله تعالى فالرهان هي القلوب التي ليس فيها غير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flying lover has lost heart and reason and is carried by divine attraction, so no pledge is demanded of him; he is overcome by God’s force, and only the destitute lover can bear the trust.
rows.anchor: فأما الطيار الذي هو عاشق مفقود القلب مسلوب العقل مجذوب السير فلا يطالب بالرهن

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that Paradise asks God to admit whoever asks for it three times, and Hell asks God to protect whoever seeks refuge from it three times; the author prays for Paradise and righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: وعن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should patiently bear the hardships of obedience and afflictions such as illness, poverty, drought, and fear.
rows.anchor: على مشاق الطاعات وما يصيبكم من الشدائد كالمرض والفقر والقحط والخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should outlast enemies in the hardships of war and their greatest enemy, the ego, in resisting desire.
rows.anchor: وغالبوا أعداء الله في الصبر على شدائد الحرب وأعدى عدوكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musābara is a particular, harder and better kind of patience, singled out after general patience because of its difficulty and excellence.
rows.anchor: والمصابرة نوع خاص من الصبر ذكر بعد الصبر على ما يجب الصبر عليه تخصيصا لشدته وصعوبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience progresses from effortful self-restraint, to resisting what blocks it, then sustained commitment, and finally complete patience without strain.
rows.anchor: ثم الاصطبار والاعتبار والالتزام ثم الصبر وهو كماله وحصوله من غير كلفة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet defines ribāṭ as thorough ablution despite hardship, frequent steps to mosques, and waiting for one prayer after another; these acts erase sins and raise ranks.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "ألا أدلكم على ما يمحو الله به الخطايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribāṭ means stationing bodies and horses at frontier posts, and keeping the self on obedience; spiritually, it is vigilance of the innermost self for divine arrivals.
rows.anchor: أبدانكم وخيولكم في النغور مترصدين وأنفسكم على الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwā means either disavowing all besides God for complete success or avoiding shameful acts to attain three stations: patience in obedience, resistance to habits, and watchful attention to divine arrivals, corresponding to law, path, and reality.
rows.anchor: واتقوه بالتبرى مما سواه لكي تفلحوا غاية الفلاح أو اتقوا القبائح لعلكم تفلحون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spiritual rank of patience is below musābara, and musābara is below ribāṭ.
rows.anchor: فعلم من هذا أن الصبر دون المصابرة والمصابرة دون المرابطة
